metadata.run_type: real end-to-end (git-mcp via stdio; benchmark-mcp not exercised — target server not running)
metadata.notes: Rules applied from skills: security-assessment (Configuration Security, GHA N/A), database-assessment (Query Anti-Patterns), code-quality-assessment (TS rules), performance-assessment (static review only). Every finding id below is a canonical `→ FINDING:` rule id from skills/*.skill.md.

findings.description: JWT secret falls back to the hardcoded default 'superSecret' when JWT_SECRET is not set (also at auth.ts:21 and token.utils.ts:4). Any deployment missing the env var accepts tokens signed with a publicly known secret — full auth bypass. Rule: security-assessment Configuration Security (jwt_secret_default_or_short → security-jwt-weak-3, critical).
findings.remediation: Remove the fallback: throw at boot if JWT_SECRET is unset. Rotate any token signed with 'superSecret'. Add a startup validation step (e.g. envalid/zod) for required env vars.

findings.description: Paginated list endpoints run prisma.article.count() and prisma.article.findMany() as two sequential awaits (getArticles :71-77 and getFeed :114-122). The count blocks the findMany, doubling DB I/O latency on the hottest read paths. Rule: database-assessment Query Anti-Patterns (sequential_count_and_findmany_on_paginated_endpoint → database-sequential-pagination-1, high).
findings.remediation: Execute both in parallel: const [articlesCount, articles] = await Promise.all([prisma.article.count({where}), prisma.article.findMany({where, ...})]). Apply to getArticles and getFeed.

evidence.snippet: const articlesCount = await prisma.article.count({...}); const articles = await prisma.article.findMany({...})

findings.description: favoritedBy: true is included in Prisma queries at 8+ call sites (:98, :101, :147, :150, :229, :232, :260, :263, :373, :376, :588, :591, :634, :637). This loads the FULL many-to-many user relation into memory only to compute article.favorited via favoritedBy.some(f => f.id === id) (:601, :647). An article with thousands of favorites OOMs the process per request. Rule: database-assessment Query Anti-Patterns (full_relation_included_to_derive_single_flag → database-overfetch-relation-1, high).
findings.remediation: Replace the include with a filtered existence check: favoritedBy: { where: { id: userId }, select: { id: true } } or use _count + a per-current-user some() subquery. favoritesCount already uses _count — extend that pattern to the favorited flag.

evidence.snippet: include: { ... favoritedBy: true ... }; article.favoritedBy.some((favorited: any) => favorited.id === id)

findings.description: No input validation exists at any API boundary: service functions take query: any / body: any (getArticles :69, and controllers pass req.query/req.body straight through). Pagination params (limit/offset), slugs and auth payloads are unvalidated. Rule: code-quality-assessment Error Handling Anti-Patterns (no_validation_at_api_boundary → code-missing-validation-4, high).
findings.remediation: Add a validation middleware (zod or class-validator) on all routes; type service inputs strictly instead of any. Validate limit/offset ranges, slug format, and required fields before they reach Prisma.

findings.description: app.use(cors()) with no options enables Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * on every route. Combined with JWT-in-localStorage frontends this widens the attack surface for cross-origin abuse. Rule: security-assessment Configuration Security (cors_allows_all_origins → security-cors-wildcard-2, medium).
findings.remediation: Configure cors({ origin: ['https://your-frontend'], credentials: true }) with an explicit allowlist; reject unknown origins.

findings.description: any is used in public/service interfaces (query: any, favorited: any in mappers at :601/:647), disabling TypeScript's safety net exactly at the API surface. Rule: code-quality-assessment Language-Specific Rules / TypeScript (any type in public API → code-any-type-6, medium).
findings.remediation: Define DTO types for query/body (e.g. ArticleQuery { tag?: string; author?: string; limit?: number; offset?: number }) and replace mapper anys with generated Prisma types.

findings.description: The global error handler returns raw err.message with HTTP 500 for unclassified errors, potentially leaking internal exception text (paths, library names) to clients. Rule: security-assessment Configuration Security (error_detail_exposed_to_client → security-error-detail-1, info).
findings.remediation: Log the full error server-side; return a generic message to the client (e.g. { status: 'error', message: 'Internal server error' }).
